title: Error Handling and Error Codes
description: Handle PrismaClientKnownRequestError, unique constraint violations (P2002), and record not found errors (P2025) cleanly.

data.text: When database operations fail (e.g. duplicate unique key, foreign key violation, connection timeout), Prisma throws structured exceptions categorized into four distinct error classes. Knowing how to parse and map these errors to user-friendly HTTP status codes is essential for backend resilience.

rows: Known error with specific database error code (P2002, P2025)
Database returned an error code not yet mapped by Prisma engine
Failed to connect to database during startup (bad credentials, host down)
Missing required fields or incorrect argument types passed to method
Record with this value already exists (e.g. duplicate email). Return HTTP 409.
Referenced parent record does not exist or cannot be deleted. Return HTTP 400.
`findUniqueOrThrow` or `update` failed to find record. Return HTTP 404.
Connection pool exhausted. Scale connection pool or inspect slow queries. Return HTTP 504.

data.title: Universal API Error Formatter
data.content: Clean error mapping for Next.js Route Handlers and Server Actions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Check for `instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to handle database constraint errors.
Never expose raw database stack traces directly to end users in production.
